identity: Utrecht University Aardwetenschappen BSc, Dutch, full time, 2026–2027 standard programme
curriculum: The degree comprises a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling space. Six level-one courses contribute 45 EC and Fieldwork 1 contributes 15 EC. The chosen surface-formation route has four level-two taught courses worth 30 EC, then two advanced taught choices and two compatible fieldwork modules worth 30 EC. The current 15 EC thesis brings the major to 135 EC. The major has 90 EC at level two or above, including 45 EC at level three. The example follows the neutral first-listed surface route and the current route page’s order for Data Analysis and Statistics, Delta Evolution and Subsurface, Coastal and River Dynamics and the Italy fieldwork pairing. The OER lists differential equations ahead of data analysis while the current route page reverses that choice. Both are explicitly permitted, so the recorded selection is valid. Profiling remains 45 EC of genuine choice, with at least 15 EC at level two or higher and no substantial overlap. No named minor is assumed.
progression: Fieldwork 1 requires 22.5 EC from first-year periods one and two by 1 March. Data Analysis and Statistics requires the first-year mathematics and statistics course. The other selected level-two taught courses require 30 first-year major EC. The selected advanced taught courses require 45 first-year major EC and 7.5 level-two major EC. The Italy fieldwork pairing requires 75 major EC including Fieldwork 1 and 15 EC of relevant level-two study by 1 March; the lowland module is taken with Source to Sink. Thesis GEO3-1323 requires all first-year courses and 7.5 EC of advanced route study outside Fieldwork 2. It has preparatory class work and an individual supervised research project, English thesis with Dutch lay summary and peer feedback, completed across two periods. The rules for 120 EC, completed Fieldwork 2 and 15 advanced EC belong to the pre-2023 thesis and are excluded from this example. BSA is 45 first-year EC, subject to individual circumstances and formal protections. Attendance and participation duties are assessed under course rules. No extra noncredit component is counted toward 180 EC.
